title: Where Benefits Meet Digital and Financial Security
summary: Employee benefits can do more than support health and retirement. Digital protection and financial tools can help families manage risks that affect their lives at home and at work.
body_markdown:
## **Protecting the Digital and Financial Lives of Working Families**


Each year, employees compare health plans and retirement options while making decisions that affect their entire household. They’re also responsible for protecting online accounts, financial information and other personal data – areas traditional benefits often don’t address. A single compromised password can lead to a drained account, a fraudulent loan, or a stolen tax return. These risks rarely appear on a benefits summary, yet they affect health, stability, and peace of mind just as much as any medical claim.


## **Where Benefits Meet Digital and Financial Security**


Norton LifeLock Benefit Solutions, the employee benefits channel of Gen, started with identity protection and digital security from LifeLock and Norton. It has since added privacy removal to strengthen preventive protection, along with tools for everyday money decisions. Employers typically offer these programs as voluntary benefits that help employees protect their devices, accounts, and personal information. Coverage can extend to the people employees care about most, not just the person on the enrollment form, reflecting how families live and how risk spreads across them. One example is Toyota Motor North America, which has partnered with Gen for more than 13 years to provide identity and digital protection benefits to its employees and their families, covering 100% of the cost and helping them navigate the digital world with greater confidence, reflecting the company’s broader commitment to financial confidence and digital safety both at home and at work.


Gen’s offerings now reach beyond online safety into everyday financial decisions and major life events.[Norton Money Workplace](https://newsroom.gendigital.com/2026-10-22-Norton-LifeLock-Benefit-Solutions-Introduces-Norton-Money-Workplace) gives employees a real-time view of their income and spending, support for student debt, education and long-term goals, access to unbiased planners, and a personal AI assistant. Earned Wage Access will give employees more control over their cash flow by letting them access wages they have already earned.


Executives face distinct risks. Cybercriminals are becoming more sophisticated, and public-facing leaders are often easier to find and target.[Norton Executive](https://us.norton.com/employee-benefits/norton-executive) gives company leaders a dedicated protection advisor, extends digital security to their families across mobile, home, and desktop devices, and provides threat intelligence focused on the risks they face.


Taken together, these offerings reflect the evolution of employee benefits, from traditional coverage to connected support for the digital, financial, and personal risks people face every day.


## **Why this matters at work**


Digital and financial threats don’t stay at home. They follow employees through every stage of life. Younger employees are building their digital footprint for the first time, midcareer employees are balancing families and finances, and employees approaching retirement face scams aimed at larger sums. Across age groups, Gen’s efficacy data suggests roughly 9% of employees are affected by identity theft each year.


When identity theft happens, resolving it can take far longer than most people expect. According to the Identity Theft Resource Center, 64% of identity crime victims who contacted the center spent more than 40 hours fixing the damage. Those hours go to phone calls, paperwork, and documentation instead of the responsibilities employees were hired to handle.


Financial pressure shows up at work, too. Nearly half of employees (46%) don’t know exactly where their money went last month, 66% have delayed a financial decision because they weren’t sure what to do, and employees spend an average of 4.84 hours a week on personal finances during work hours. A scam call impersonating a bank can drain an account, and a stolen tax return can delay refunds and require lengthy restoration.


These threats are also constant. Gen’s Employee Benefits channel seeks to address them across three areas: identity and digital protection for employees and their families, financial wellness tools that help employees manage and grow their paychecks, and executive digital protection for leaders who are often easier to find and target.


## **Why this channel matters for Gen**


Gen has served employers through this channel for over 17 years, and it has become one of the company’s thriving growth segments. As employers place more weight on lifestyle benefits, they’re looking for protections that fit how their people actually live, and digital and financial security now belong in that category.


Our offerings draw on the best of Norton, LifeLock, and MoneyLion, bringing together our portfolio across the four pillars that guide our strategy: identity, privacy, security, and financial wellness. That breadth matters because employees rarely face one threat at a time, and a benefit that addresses only one leaves gaps. Delivered as a trusted package, these protections build relationships that renew year after year.


Today, our benefit programs serve thousands of employers and over 2.3 million households, including over a third of the Fortune 500 as well as many small and mid-sized businesses. That reach reflects a simple reality: digital and financial risks can affect anyone, in any industry and at any stage of life. Protection isn’t a once-a-year conversation tied to benefits enrollment. It matters every day.


Our goal is to make protection a natural part of how companies care for their people, alongside health and retirement benefits. When employees feel more secure in their personal lives, they can focus on the work in front of them.
